tagline: A cloud drive that keeps your files in your own Telegram, GitHub or S3, with an AI sidekick.
summary: BYOS is a drive cut in half. Postgres remembers everything about your files: names, folders, versions, tags, links. The actual bytes go to storage you already own. Telegram sign-in doubles as storage setup. Then there's Bao, an AI agent on your own LLM key that answers with receipts and asks before rearranging anything.

features.name: Sign in with Telegram
features.summary: One Telegram code makes your account and plugs in your storage.
features.description: Enter a username, password and phone number. Telegram sends a code, and that's your account and storage sorted. You stay signed in for 30 days. Later a password is enough, unless you've killed your Telegram sessions since. Then it asks for a fresh code.
features.underTheHood: No user exists until the code checks out, so the half-finished login rides in the browser as a Fernet-encrypted ticket that expires after 600 s. The server keeps no pending state. After that: a 15-minute access token living only in React state, plus a refresh token in an httpOnly cookie that rotates on every use.

steps.label: enters phone
steps.narration: You pick a username and password and type your number. India is first in the country list, for reasons.

steps.label: signup details
steps.narration: The username gets checked, the password gets Argon2-hashed, and both go into the ticket. The database hasn't heard of you yet.

steps.label: asks for a code
steps.narration: A fresh Telethon client asks Telegram to send you a login code.

steps.label: encrypted ticket
steps.narration: Your browser holds an encrypted ticket it can't read. It has 10 minutes to come back with the code.

steps.label: sends the code
steps.narration: You enter the code. Got two-step verification on? Then it asks for that password too.

steps.label: creates user + storage
steps.narration: Now you exist. Your account and Telegram storage are created together in one transaction, with the session string encrypted.

steps.label: token + refresh cookie
steps.narration: You get a 15-minute token kept in memory plus a refresh cookie. Reload and the cookie quietly fetches a new one.

keyFiles: apps/api/src/byos_api/auth/telegram.py — ticket-based multi-step MTProto login and account/storage upsert
apps/api/src/byos_api/auth/service.py — issuing, rotating and revoking refresh tokens; password login
apps/web/lib/auth-context.tsx — in-memory token, refresh-and-retry on 401, reconnect notice

features.name: Uploads to your storage
features.summary: Files land in your Telegram, GitHub or S3. BYOS just remembers where.
features.description: Telegram is connected the moment you sign in. A GitHub repo or any S3-compatible bucket can be added in settings. Drop files and they upload three at a time. If a token dies, only that storage gets flagged, and a banner tells you which.
features.underTheHood: Every backend implements one StorageProvider protocol. Telegram uploads land in Saved Messages, and BYOS keeps the message id, never Telegram's file_id, which expires. GitHub files become release assets on one prerelease per day, dodging the 1,000-assets-per-release cap. GitHub and S3 want the size up front, so uploads spool to memory, then disk, while hashing.

steps.label: drops files
steps.narration: You drag in a pile of files. Three upload at a time, over XMLHttpRequest, because fetch still can't report upload progress.

steps.label: multipart upload
steps.narration: The upload shows up with your login token. A script using an API key would need the files:write scope.

steps.label: validates and routes
steps.narration: Too big, blocked extension or not your folder? Rejected before a single byte moves. Then it picks which storage gets it.

steps.label: streams the bytes
steps.narration: Bytes stream to your storage in 1 MiB bites. If the provider complains, the error says which account it was.

steps.label: into Saved Messages
steps.narration: The file is posted to your own Saved Messages as a document. You could scroll back and find it there yourself.

steps.label: writes the record
steps.narration: Uploaded the same file twice? The new copy is deleted and you get the old one. A failed save cleans up too.

steps.label: the new file
steps.narration: The file pops into your list without a full refresh, and a file.created webhook goes out in the background.

keyFiles: apps/api/src/byos_api/storage/base.py — StorageProvider protocol, error types, tags_account
apps/api/src/byos_api/storage/telegram.py — TelegramClientPool and Saved Messages provider
apps/api/src/byos_api/storage/github.py — release-asset provider with daily releases
apps/api/src/byos_api/storage/s3.py — boto3 provider with error translation
apps/api/src/byos_api/files/router.py — upload_file: validation, idempotency, orphan cleanup
apps/web/app/(app)/dashboard/page.tsx — Drive UI and the upload worker pool
apps/web/components/settings/storage.tsx — connecting GitHub/S3 and choosing the default

features.name: Plain-English search
features.summary: Cmd+K, then type "pdfs from last week" like a normal person.
features.description: The palette shows your recent files before you type anything. It takes operators like type:pdf, size:>2mb and in:reports, or plain phrases like "pdfs from last week larger than 2mb invoice". Searching never bothers your storage provider.
features.underTheHood: One regex chops up the query, known operators become filters, and a set of plain rules turns words like "pdfs" or "last week" into MIME types and date ranges. No AI involved, despite living in a folder called ai. Whatever's left goes to Postgres full-text search, with a trigram index on names for half-typed words.

steps.label: Cmd+K query
steps.narration: You hit Cmd+K, see your recents and start typing. The search fires once you pause.

steps.label: the query
steps.narration: If this came from an API key, it needs files:read and counts against that key's rate limit.

steps.label: parses the query
steps.narration: `pdfs from last week >2mb invoice` becomes: PDFs, a date range, a minimum size, and the word 'invoice'.

steps.label: tsvector + trigram
steps.narration: The leftover word is matched against the full-text index or a partial name match, best matches first.

steps.label: ranked results
steps.narration: Up to 100 results come back, each with its folder, tags and star.

steps.label: jumps to the file
steps.narration: Pick one and you're there. It also goes into recents for next time.

keyFiles: apps/api/src/byos_api/ai/nl_search.py — operator and natural-language query parser
apps/api/alembic/versions/0001_initial.py — pg_trgm, the generated search_vector, GIN indexes

features.name: Links that survive replacement
features.summary: Share /you/resume once, swap the file whenever. Link stays put.
features.description: Pick a username, then give any file a link like /{username}/{slug}. Upload a new version and everyone with the link gets it at the same URL. Old versions stick around, and restoring one is instant. Re-uploading the exact same file does nothing.
features.underTheHood: Telegram messages and GitHub release assets can't be edited, so the storage protocol has no replace at all. A replace uploads new bytes, adds version N+1 and moves a pointer, in one transaction. The ETag is the version's SHA-256, so new content at an old URL gets noticed and unchanged content gets a 304.

steps.label: replaces resume.pdf
steps.narration: You hit Replace on resume.pdf, the one you already sent everyone as /alex/resume.

steps.label: new file arrives
steps.narration: BYOS checks you own it and finds which storage it already lives on. Same size and extension checks as any upload.

steps.label: stores new bytes
steps.narration: Telegram can't edit a message, so the new version goes up as a brand new Saved Messages document.

steps.label: moves version pointer
steps.narration: Same hash as before? Nothing happens. Otherwise a new version row goes in and the pointer quietly moves over.

steps.label: opens /alex/resume
steps.narration: Later someone opens /alex/resume. The limit is 120 requests per 60 s per IP, unless Redis is down. Then nobody's counting.

steps.label: fetches the bytes
steps.narration: The old ETag no longer matches. BYOS grabs the first chunk before sending headers, so a missing file is an honest 404.

steps.label: new file, same URL
steps.narration: They get the new PDF at the old URL. Open it again and it's a 304.

keyFiles: apps/api/src/byos_api/aliases/router.py — owner CRUD and the public resolve_alias route
apps/api/src/byos_api/streaming.py — stream_object: first-chunk check, ETag/304, error mapping

features.name: Public folder pages
features.summary: Share a whole folder as a page anyone can browse.
features.description: Give a folder a link and visitors get a public page where they can open subfolders and view or download files. They can't wander outside the folder you shared. A link that doesn't exist gets the 404 page instead of a suspiciously empty folder.
features.underTheHood: Hitting the API URL of a folder link returns a 302 to the Next.js page. That page calls /public routes, and each one works out every folder inside the share, then rejects any id that isn't on the list. Guessing ids gets you nowhere.

steps.label: shares a folder
steps.narration: You pick a slug for the folder. You need a username first, since links live under /{username}/.

steps.label: creates the link
steps.narration: The slug gets checked: lowercase letters, digits and dashes. If the folder already has a link, you get a 409.

steps.label: saves the link
steps.narration: The database itself makes sure each link points at exactly one thing and each slug is used once.

steps.label: opens the link
steps.narration: A visitor opens the link. The API sees it's a folder and bounces them to the web app with a 302.

steps.label: opens folder page
steps.narration: The public page shows breadcrumbs and a list of folders and files.

steps.label: lists one level
steps.narration: Each click loads one level. Ask for a folder outside the share and the request fails.

steps.label: streams a file
steps.narration: Opening a file checks it's inside the share, then streams it. Owner's credentials broken? The visitor just sees 'unavailable'.

keyFiles: apps/api/src/byos_api/aliases/router.py — public_api_router (/public/...) and the redirect for folder links

features.name: Expiring share links
features.summary: Links that self-destruct after 1 to 365 days.
features.description: Make as many extra links to a file as you like. Each one counts its downloads, can be revoked any time, and returns 410 Gone once it expires. They always serve the latest version. Password-protected shares existed once and got removed.
features.underTheHood: Each share is a random token with an expiry date and a download counter. Opening /s/{token} checks the date, bumps the counter and streams the file through the same code as permanent links. Revoking just deletes the row, and deleting it twice is fine.

steps.label: sets expiry
steps.narration: You pick how many days the link should live, anywhere from 1 to 365.

steps.label: asks for a link
steps.narration: BYOS checks the file is yours and rolls a random token.

steps.label: stores token
steps.narration: The share is saved with its expiry date and a download count of zero.

steps.label: opens the link
steps.narration: Someone opens it. 120 requests per 60 s per IP, unless Redis is down, in which case nobody's counting.

steps.label: checks expiry, counts
steps.narration: Expired? 410 Gone. Otherwise the download counter ticks up by one.

steps.label: streams the file
steps.narration: The bytes come straight from the owner's storage, with the content hash as the ETag.

keyFiles: apps/api/src/byos_api/shares/service.py — create, resolve, expiry, download counting
apps/api/src/byos_api/shares/router.py — owner CRUD and public GET /s/{token}

features.name: Missing files and duplicates
features.summary: Catches files deleted behind BYOS's back, plus exact duplicates.
features.description: Your bytes live in your storage, so you can delete them there without BYOS knowing. The Missing page scans every file and lists the ones that vanished. The Duplicates page groups identical files, whatever they're called, so you can bin the extras.
features.underTheHood: The scan asks each provider whether the object still exists, without downloading it: get_messages on Telegram, head_object on S3, an asset lookup on GitHub. If Telegram says slow down, it stops and returns what it has. Duplicates come free, since every upload already recorded its SHA-256.

steps.label: runs a scan
steps.narration: On the Missing page you hit scan. Time to see what you deleted from Telegram and forgot about.

steps.label: check everything
steps.narration: BYOS loads every file along with the storage account it lives on.

steps.label: still there?
steps.narration: Each provider is asked whether the file is still there. Nothing gets downloaded.

steps.label: get_messages
steps.narration: A message that's gone, or has no file attached, means missing. If Telegram rate-limits, the scan ends early with partial results.

steps.label: flags the missing
steps.narration: Missing files get flagged. Files that came back from the dead get unflagged.

steps.label: missing + duplicates
steps.narration: You get a list of missing files to clear out, and duplicates grouped by hash.

keyFiles: apps/api/src/byos_api/streaming.py — the on_missing callback when a download hits FileNotFoundError

features.name: Indexing, even of scans
features.summary: Your own model reads every file, even scanned PDFs and photos.
features.description: Index everything or tick specific files, and watch progress live. Scans and photos have no text, so those pages go to your own vision model. Normal PDFs cost nothing extra. Re-running only touches changed files, and index data unused for 30 days expires.
features.underTheHood: pypdf pulls text out page by page. A page with under 80 characters is probably a scan, so it's rendered at 2x and sent for transcription, up to 20 per file. The first refusal stops that, since it usually means the model can't see. Text is cut into 1,800-character chunks with 200 overlap, then embedded.

steps.label: picks files
steps.narration: You pick what to index. The panel already knows which files are up to date.

steps.label: start indexing
steps.narration: This needs a real login, not an API key, plus an LLM key with an embedding model.

steps.label: downloads the file
steps.narration: Files that changed get downloaded from your storage. Anything over 25 MB is skipped, and you're told why.

steps.label: reads the scans
steps.narration: Near-empty pages get rendered and sent to your vision model. One refusal and it stops, so you don't pay for every page.

steps.label: embeds chunks
steps.narration: Text is sliced into 1,800-character chunks and embedded. If the provider says slow down, it waits as told and tries again.

steps.label: saves the vectors
steps.narration: Old chunks for that file are thrown out and the new ones go in, one row per chunk.

steps.label: streams progress
steps.narration: Progress lines trickle in as each file finishes, with the occasional 'warn' and a reason.

keyFiles: apps/api/src/byos_api/ai/extract.py — pypdf text extraction, sparse_pages, MAX_CHARS
apps/api/src/byos_api/ai/vision.py — page rendering with pypdfium2 and vision transcription
apps/api/src/byos_api/ai/semantic.py — ensure_embedded and the chunk cache
apps/web/components/byok/index-panel.tsx — file/folder picker with live progress

features.name: Ask your drive
features.summary: Ask anything across your documents. Bao answers and shows receipts.
features.description: Bao reads through your files before answering, with source chips under the reply. Click one and the PDF opens beside it with the quote highlighted. Ask something vague like "my salary in June" with two years of payslips, and it asks which June.
features.underTheHood: Bao ends each answer with [source: file | exact words] lines, and citations.py keeps a quote only if those words really appear in that file. Made-up quotes quietly vanish. Retrieval then hands out each file's best chunk first, so a question spanning ten documents doesn't come back citing just one.

steps.label: asks a question
steps.narration: You type "What was my net pay in June 2026?" and hit enter. Nothing clever has happened yet.

steps.label: question goes to Bao
steps.narration: Your API key is decrypted before the stream starts, so a bad key gets a clean error, not a mess halfway through.

steps.label: asks the model
steps.narration: Your model gets at least 8,192 output tokens, so a reasoning model can't think itself out of budget. It decides to search.

steps.label: go search
steps.narration: The search query gets embedded with your key's embedding model. Optionally Bao writes a fake answer first (HyDE) and searches with that.

steps.label: ranks chunk vectors
steps.narration: Every chunk you've indexed gets scored in numpy in one go. Getting picked also resets the chunk's expiry clock.

steps.label: answer + receipts
steps.narration: The model answers and cites its sources. Any quote that isn't actually in the file gets thrown out before you see it.

steps.label: highlights the quote
steps.narration: Click a source and the PDF opens next to the answer, with the quoted words highlighted right there on the page.

keyFiles: apps/api/src/byos_api/ai/agent.py — run(): the tool loop, system prompt, clarify rules, separating reasoning from the answer
apps/api/src/byos_api/ai/rag.py — retrieve(): rewrite, HyDE, rerank, CRAG, _diversify
apps/api/src/byos_api/ai/semantic.py — chunk embedding cache and numpy cosine ranking
apps/api/src/byos_api/ai/citations.py — parsing [source: …] lines and verifying quotes
apps/web/components/byok/drive-chat.tsx — composer, slash commands, splitting the stream into events and text
apps/web/components/byok/pdf-view.tsx — pdf.js rendering with quote highlights

features.name: Agent plans you approve
features.summary: Bao plans the cleanup. You decide what it's allowed to touch.
features.description: Say "tidy my downloads" or run /organize. Bao drafts every move, rename and new folder, flags the scary ones, and draws your drive as it'll look afterwards. Four permission modes, from Read only to Full access, set how much it does without asking.
features.underTheHood: Read tools run right away. Write tools may get queued, and queued writes are reported to the model as done, so it can plan "make Finance, move 12 files in" in one pass. Folders that don't exist yet are $new:N placeholders. The plan lives on the server, so Apply runs only what the model proposed.

steps.label: /organize
steps.narration: In Ask-first mode you run /organize, maybe with options like `rename by:year depth:1`.

steps.label: organize request
steps.narration: Bao spots an organising job, grabs an inventory of your whole drive and gets 30 steps instead of the usual 10.

steps.label: reads the drive
steps.narration: Read tools run straight away. A file called scan_0032.pdf gets judged by its contents, since its name is no help at all.

steps.label: proposes changes
steps.narration: The model says "create Finance, move these in". In Ask mode nothing actually happens. Bao nods and writes it down.

steps.label: plan + tree
steps.narration: The plan is saved as pending and streamed to you, along with a tree of what your drive will look like after.

steps.label: you hit Apply
steps.narration: You press Apply. The server runs its own stored copy of the plan, so the browser can't slip in extra actions.

steps.label: runs each action
steps.narration: Each action runs through the same code as the regular Drive UI. It's all metadata, so nothing moves in Telegram.

keyFiles: apps/api/src/byos_api/ai/modes.py — the Mode enum (read_only, ask, auto, full) and runs_now
apps/api/src/byos_api/ai/tools.py — READ/WRITE tool schemas, $new references, apply_action
apps/api/src/byos_api/ai/organize.py — inventory, brief, excluded_tools, preview tree, fix_brief
apps/web/components/byok/plan-card.tsx — plan list with apply, discard and revise
apps/web/components/byok/plan-tree.tsx — diagram of the drive after the plan

features.name: Chat with one file
features.summary: Ask questions about the file you're looking at.
features.description: Preview a PDF, text file or image and an AI panel sits right next to it. Pick a key and a prompt and chat with that one file. These chats aren't stored on BYOS servers; they live in your browser. Long documents work too.
features.underTheHood: The server keeps no state: the browser resends up to 20 turns of history every time. Short documents go into the prompt whole, up to 120,000 characters. Longer ones get embedded on the spot and only the 6 most relevant chunks are sent. No embedding model? It falls back to plain word overlap.

steps.label: asks about a file
steps.narration: You ask the side panel a question. Earlier messages come back out of localStorage.

steps.label: question + history
steps.narration: Your question, the history, and your chosen key and prompt all go to the API together.

steps.label: downloads the file
steps.narration: The file comes down from your storage (25 MB max) and its text is pulled out, scans included.

steps.label: picks relevant chunks
steps.narration: Long document? Only the 6 most relevant chunks make the cut. No embeddings means old-school word matching instead.

steps.label: asks your model
steps.narration: Your prompt, the document bits and your question go to your provider's chat endpoint, streaming on.

steps.label: streams tokens
steps.narration: Tokens are passed straight through. The panel renders Markdown as it arrives and saves the chat locally.

keyFiles: apps/api/src/byos_api/ai/retrieval.py — chunk_text and the lexical top_chunks fallback
apps/web/components/dashboard/ai-panel.tsx — preview-side chat with a localStorage history

features.name: API keys and webhooks
features.summary: Script your drive with scoped API keys and signed webhooks.
features.description: Create keys like byosk_<prefix>_<secret>, shown once, with read or write scopes per resource and an optional expiry. Webhooks fire when files are created, replaced or deleted, signed with HMAC-SHA256. A leaked key can't mint more keys or read your storage credentials.
features.underTheHood: Only a hash of each key is stored. Webhook URLs pointing at private or loopback IPs are refused, and redirects are never followed, so nobody can bounce a delivery to an internal address. Delivery is fire-and-forget: one asyncio task, a 5 s timeout, no retries. If your endpoint is down at that moment, tough luck.

steps.label: creates a key
steps.narration: You name a key, tick scopes like files:write and maybe set an expiry. The max is 3,650 days. Optimistic.

steps.label: saves the key
steps.narration: Only the hash is stored, and you see the full key exactly once. Copy it now.

steps.label: Bearer byosk_…
steps.narration: Your script calls POST /files with the key in the Authorization header.

steps.label: checks key + scope
steps.narration: The key is found by prefix and its hash compared. A POST needs files:write, and Redis counts calls per key.

steps.label: runs the upload
steps.narration: From here it's the same upload path as the web app. The API doesn't care who's asking.

steps.label: emit file.created
steps.narration: A file.created event gets handed to a background task. The upload doesn't wait around for it.

steps.label: signed POST
steps.narration: Your webhook gets a signed POST with a 5 s timeout. If that fails, it's logged and forgotten.

keyFiles: apps/api/src/byos_api/apikeys/service.py — key format, hashing, ALL_SCOPES, MAX_ACTIVE_KEYS
docs/DEVELOPERS.md — developer guide with the signature verification snippet

nodes.label: You
nodes.summary: You. The one with the files and the LLM key.
nodes.details: You own the storage accounts and the LLM key. Everything you do goes through the web app, after signing in with Telegram or a password.

nodes.label: Link Visitor
nodes.summary: Anyone you sent a link to. No account needed.
nodes.details: Opens /{username}/{slug} or /s/{token}. Files stream inline and folder links bounce to the web app. Every public route is rate-limited per IP.

nodes.label: Web App
nodes.summary: The Drive, the Bao chat, settings and public folder pages.
nodes.details: A client-rendered Next.js app that talks to the API through a typed SDK. The access token lives only in React state, and a refresh cookie brings it back on reload. Preferences like theme and click sounds stay on your device.
keyFiles: apps/web/components/byok/drive-chat.tsx — composer, slash commands, stream handling
nodes.interesting: Bao's answers and control events share one plain-text stream, split by the ASCII record separator. No WebSockets needed, and sources survive a reload.

nodes.label: Your Scripts
nodes.summary: Your scripts, calling the API with byosk_ keys.
nodes.details: Sends `Bearer byosk_<prefix>_<secret>` and gets only what the key's scopes allow, at a per-key rate limit. Can also receive signed file events, which it should verify before trusting.
keyFiles: docs/DEVELOPERS.md — API reference, scopes, webhook verification

nodes.label: API Gateway
nodes.summary: The FastAPI app. Every request walks through here.
nodes.details: Handles auth, scope checks, rate limits and error mapping. When your storage credentials die, it says which provider and account, so the app knows exactly what to ask you to fix. API docs are switched off in production.
keyFiles: apps/api/src/byos_api/main.py — app factory, error handlers, the daily cleanup task
apps/api/src/byos_api/core/ratelimit.py — fixed-window limiter that fails open
nodes.interesting: It's on every request, but the walkthroughs only draw it when it does real work. Otherwise it would be on every single arrow.

nodes.label: Auth & Keys
nodes.summary: Logins, sessions and API keys. The bouncer.
nodes.details: Turns each request into a full session or a scoped API key. Runs the Telegram login, hands out 15-minute access tokens and 30-day refresh tokens that rotate on every use. Security events get logged with IPs hashed.
keyFiles: apps/api/src/byos_api/audit/recorder.py — audit writer that never raises
nodes.interesting: A password login never talks to Telegram, so it checks your Telegram session is still alive first. Dead session? You get a fresh code.

nodes.label: Metadata Engine
nodes.summary: Everything about your files, except the files.
nodes.details: Folders, versions, tags, search, duplicates and missing files all live here. It picks which storage gets an upload, hands the bytes to the adapters and cleans up if saving fails. Bao's write tools call this same code.
nodes.interesting: The duplicate check waits until after upload, since the hash isn't known until the bytes are read. So a retried upload gets stored, spotted and deleted.

nodes.label: Links Service
nodes.summary: Permanent links, shared folders and expiring shares.
nodes.details: Owners create links here. Visitors use them without logging in, at 120 requests per 60 s per IP. Files stream inline, folder links redirect to the web app, and expired shares return 410.
keyFiles: apps/api/src/byos_api/aliases/router.py — owner CRUD, public resolver, /public folder API
nodes.interesting: The ETag is the content hash. Same file as last time? You get a 304 and Telegram never even hears about it.

nodes.label: Storage Adapters
nodes.summary: One plug shape, three sockets: Telegram, GitHub and S3.
nodes.details: Each adapter translates its backend's errors into two plain types, one of which means 'your credentials are dead'. Credentials are stored encrypted. Disconnecting wipes them but keeps the record, so files come back if you reconnect.
nodes.interesting: There's no replace method. Telegram and GitHub can't edit uploads anyway, so a replace is upload new, add a version, move a pointer. Same on every backend.

nodes.label: Webhook Dispatcher
nodes.summary: Sends signed file events without holding up your request.
nodes.details: A background task POSTs one signed JSON body to every matching webhook, with a 5 s timeout. Failures are logged and dropped, and a restart loses anything pending. A proper queue (arq) is installed, but nothing runs it yet.
nodes.interesting: Redirects are never followed. Otherwise a URL that passed the private-IP check could just redirect the delivery to an internal address.

nodes.label: Bao Agent
nodes.summary: The AI agent. Answers questions, drafts plans, waits for your OK.
nodes.details: Runs each chat turn as up to 10 model steps, or 30 when organising. Read tools run right away. Write tools run or get queued depending on your permission mode. Plans can be applied, discarded, revised or fixed.
nodes.interesting: Plans live on the server, so Apply can only run what the model proposed. In Auto mode a plan can be half done, the rest waiting on you.

nodes.label: Index & Retrieval
nodes.summary: Reads your files, embeds them, finds the right bits later.
nodes.details: Pulls text out page by page, sends nearly blank pages to your vision model, then chunks and embeds everything. At question time it can rewrite the query, rerank, and search again if results look weak. It also fact-checks Bao's quotes.
keyFiles: apps/api/src/byos_api/ai/semantic.py — embedding cache and cosine ranking
nodes.interesting: There's no vector database. Embeddings are plain float arrays in Postgres and numpy does one big multiply per query. The stack stays at exactly one database.

nodes.label: LLM Client
nodes.summary: Talks to whatever AI provider your key points at.
nodes.details: Speaks the OpenAI-compatible format to any base URL. When a provider rejects a parameter, it adjusts and retries up to 3 times, then remembers the fix. Bad keys, dead endpoints and rate limits each get their own error.
keyFiles: apps/api/tests/test_llm_params.py — tests for adapting rejected parameters
nodes.interesting: Nobody documents which reasoning-effort levels a model accepts. So the client reads the allowed values out of the provider's error message and picks the closest one.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL
nodes.summary: The source of truth. Everything except the bytes.
nodes.details: 19 tables across 25 migrations, covering users, files, versions, links, keys, AI chats, chunks and plans. Files get a full-text index plus a trigram index on names. Production runs on Supabase in Mumbai.
nodes.interesting: The deploy notes say the API-to-database round trip is the real cost per request, so every hosting option is picked by how close it sits to this database.

nodes.label: Redis
nodes.summary: Optional. Rate limits and a tiny cache.
nodes.details: Counts requests per IP or key in fixed windows and caches the storage overview for 30 s. Runs locally in docker-compose. Production skips it for now, so rate limits are basically off there.
nodes.interesting: Everything fails open. If Redis dies you lose rate limiting and caching, and the API carries on as if nothing happened.

nodes.label: Telegram
nodes.summary: Your Telegram account. Your login and your default storage.
nodes.details: Files go to Saved Messages as documents and are fetched by message id on every download. Up to 2 GB per file, 4 GB with Premium. Hit Telegram's flood limits and you get a polite 'try again in N s'.
nodes.interesting: Log out every session from the Telegram app and BYOS gets logged out too. It notices, drops its client and asks you to sign in again.

nodes.label: GitHub Releases
nodes.summary: Files stored as release assets in a repo you own.
nodes.details: BYOS creates the repo (private by default) and uploads files as assets on a daily prerelease. Why not commits? A committed file caps out at 100 MB, bloats the history and never truly goes away.
nodes.interesting: GitHub sends your token's expiry date on every response. BYOS reads it so it can warn you before a fine-grained token dies.

nodes.label: S3 Bucket
nodes.summary: Any S3-compatible bucket: AWS, R2, B2, MinIO.
nodes.details: Objects go to <prefix><uuid>/<safe filename> through boto3 in worker threads, with up to 3 retries. A dead key and a key missing one permission get different error messages, which saves some head-scratching.

nodes.label: Your LLM
nodes.summary: Your own OpenAI-compatible endpoint, running on your own key.
nodes.details: Does chat, streaming, tool calls, embeddings, vision transcription and model listing. Your key is stored encrypted and only decrypted to make these calls.

nodes.label: Keep-warm Cron
nodes.summary: A cron that pokes the servers so they don't fall asleep.
nodes.details: A Google Apps Script pings the web app and the API every 5 minutes, because Render's free tier naps after about 15 idle minutes. Its own notes admit two services need about 1,490 instance-hours a month, against 750 free.

zones.label: Client
zones.description: You, your visitors, the web app and your scripts.

zones.label: BYOS API
zones.description: One FastAPI app, with Bao living inside it.

zones.label: Data
zones.description: Postgres holds everything but the bytes. Redis is optional.

zones.label: Your Storage
zones.description: Where your bytes actually live. Accounts you own.

zones.label: Third-party
zones.description: Your LLM endpoint and a cron that keeps things awake.

edges.label: uses the app
edges.payload: Clicks, drag-and-drop files, chat messages, Cmd+K queries
edges.details: Works on desktop and phone. On phones the Drive gets a bottom tab bar.

edges.label: REST + Bearer JWT
edges.payload: JSON, or multipart/form-data for uploads; Authorization: Bearer <access JWT>
edges.details: Sends the refresh cookie along. On a 401 it refreshes once and tries again.

edges.label: resolves principal
edges.payload: Bearer credential → Principal{user, auth_type, scopes, key_prefix}
edges.details: byosk_ keys get hashed and looked up. Anything else is treated as a JWT.

edges.label: /auth/* login
edges.details: 20 requests per 60 s per IP. Hands back a token and a fresh cookie.

edges.label: send code, sign in
edges.details: A fresh Telethon client for every step. Flood limits become a 429.

edges.label: users, tokens, keys
edges.details: Account and storage are created in one transaction. Audit logs use their own session.

edges.label: files and folders
edges.payload: Calls scoped to the owner, e.g. upload, search, move, verify
edges.details: Every route checks scopes and the per-key rate limit first.

edges.label: /files, /folders
edges.details: Really goes through the gateway. The walkthroughs just skip drawing it.

edges.label: metadata + search
edges.payload: files, file_versions, folders, tags; recursive CTEs; websearch_to_tsquery + ILIKE
edges.details: An upload's rows and its version pointer are saved in one commit.

edges.label: upload / download
edges.details: Uploads move in 1 MiB chunks. Errors come back tagged with which account broke.

edges.label: Saved Messages I/O
edges.details: One pooled client per session. A revoked session gets kicked out of the pool.

edges.label: release assets
edges.payload: Asset upload to uploads.github.com; asset GET following the redirect
edges.details: Release ids are cached per repo per day. A 401 means the token got revoked.

edges.label: put / get object
edges.details: boto3 in worker threads, retrying up to 3 times.

edges.label: storage_accounts
edges.payload: Encrypted credentials and config; status updates
edges.details: Flagging a broken account uses its own session.

edges.label: manage links
edges.payload: POST/GET/PATCH/DELETE /aliases and /shares; GET /public/... from the folder page
edges.details: API keys need the aliases scope. Public routes get the per-IP limit.

edges.label: opens a link
edges.details: Can return 200, 304, 302 for folders, 404, or 410 for an expired share.

edges.label: shared folder page
edges.payload: GET /{username}/{slug} on the web app after the API's 302
edges.details: Links that don't exist get the 404 page.

edges.label: resolve links
edges.details: Shares count their downloads here. A missing file gets flagged on the way.

edges.label: stream_object
edges.payload: First chunk fetched before headers, then a StreamingResponse with the hash as ETag
edges.details: With public=True, broken owner credentials show the visitor a 503.

edges.label: public rate limit
edges.details: Fixed 60 s window. If Redis fails, requests go through anyway.

edges.label: limits + cache
edges.details: Fails open. No Redis, no problem.

edges.label: /ai/agent/*
edges.payload: {conversation_id, key_id, message, mode, strategies, organize?, revises?, fixes?}; plans/{id}/apply|discard
edges.details: Control events are JSON tucked into the answer text behind a record-separator byte.

edges.label: chat_tools steps
edges.details: Not streamed, because every provider chops up tool-call deltas differently.

edges.label: read and write tools
edges.details: Writes use the exact same functions as the REST API.

edges.label: search_content
edges.details: Same retrieval pipeline as RAG chat, with this turn's add-ons.

edges.label: plans and messages
edges.details: A plan only moves forward: pending, then applied or discarded.

edges.label: /ai/index, /ai/chat
edges.details: Indexing needs a real login. API keys are turned away.

edges.label: downloads for extraction
edges.details: Files already embedded at their current version are skipped.

edges.label: embed / transcribe
edges.payload: Chunks → vectors; page PNGs → text; rewrite, HyDE and rerank prompts
edges.details: Retries up to 3 times on a 429 or a network hiccup.

edges.label: ai_file_chunks
edges.details: Ranking happens in numpy, not in the database.

edges.label: OpenAI-compatible calls
edges.details: Rejected parameters get fixed and retried up to 3 times.

edges.label: emit file.*
edges.details: Fire and forget. The request moves on immediately.

edges.label: loads webhooks
edges.details: Uses its own session, since the request is already over by then.

edges.label: signed POST
edges.details: 5 s timeout, no redirects, no retries. One shot.

edges.label: Bearer byosk_ key
edges.details: 120 requests per 60 s per key. Admin routes return 403.

edges.label: GET /ping
edges.details: Every 5 minutes. Skips the database and auth entirely.

edges.label: GET /
edges.details: Every 5 minutes, just to keep the lights on.
